# SPIE Student Chapter

- [Start](https://www.eafit.edu.co/)
- [Exa](https://www.eafit.edu.co/exa)

- SPIE Student Chapter

###### Us

SPIE is an international organization dedicated to the study of optics and photonics. The EAFIT University chapter is the only one in the entire community comprised of undergraduate students and focused on community outreach. Similarly, within the university, SPIE is the only student group that accepts graduate students.

###### Our goal

Through science, we seek the social development and personal growth of young people through scientific experience, fostering the ideal that everyone can engage in science by providing a didactic approach to new ways of thinking. We aim to break down mental paradigms to create new perspectives, using science to broaden our understanding of the social context.

##### Internal organization

###### Marketing

This is the committee for creativity, continuous learning, and leadership development; they are the most active! Remember, you don't need to be a design expert to be on it.

###### Logistics

This is the organizing committee; they manage the spaces for events and provide us with the necessary tools for the chapter's work.

###### Experiments

Their goal is to plan and experiment to bring science to others; they are responsible for conducting experiments and creating events with the help of the other committees to promote science.

###### Human Resource Management

They are the ones who create the family atmosphere within the chapter by focusing on coexistence.

## Events

###### Activities

[![Image of Dumb Science activities](https://universidadeafit.widen.net/content/863ab6b6-256a-4ada-be9e-57425c3efb1b/web/focus-1.jpg?crop=yes&k=c&w=1920&h=788&itok=OQnj7Ly7)](https://www.eafit.edu.co/exa/estudiantes/grupos/spie)

**Some of the activities carried out by the student chapter are:**

Organize informative meetings or academic talks for students or teachers led by a professor from the department.

Organize informative meetings or discussion forums on optics for university students and external participants.

Invite speakers from academia or industry.

Conduct visits to optical industry facilities.

Invite students and professors to visit the University's optics laboratories.

Promote the study of science among pre-university and lower grade students: developing workshops, organizing science fairs, among other activities.

Invite and sponsor international speakers to give talks aimed at young students and professionals.
